I am now considering a counter-trade. I want cash and cannot give away Park Place or New York. Boardwalk is mortgaged, but pairing it with my existing Park Place would create a dark blue monopoly without needing New York. I rejected earlier offers for Boardwalk because they required too much cash.

p3 has no second complete monopoly. Their pink set is missing States, their red set is missing Illinois, and their green set is missing Pennsylvania. p2 holds St. Charles and Virginia, plus Kentucky and Indiana, but both are incomplete.

The opponent holds all four railroads, two orange properties, and the mortgaged Boardwalk. I should prefer that neither opponent bankrupts to p3.

The opponent has only $48, so no counter could extract meaningful cash from them. They need their four railroads as their sole income stream and will not give them up cheaply. No counter that avoids giving away Park Place or New York is viable. I am now considering whether a clearly favorable counter-trade might be accepted out of desperation.

A cash-only offer for Boardwalk would be rejected, wasting an exchange. One house on dark blue would leave only $89, making the set too weak to survive hotel hits. I will reject the trade outright.

I am now checking whether any counter-trade is worth making. The yellow monopoly would generate only modest rent, and the opponent will not give up their four railroads for cash.

No counter-trade is viable. The opponent lacks any property that would complete my sets, and they will not accept a cash-only offer for my orange properties. I will reject the trade outright.

I will reject the trade. I will keep my reasoning brief and avoid revealing too much cash math, since p3 is watching.
